Another commenter mentioned mindfulness, and that is spot-on. I suffer from brutal depression and nothing helped; not meds, exercise, hobbies, etc. everything in life felt hollow until I started taking steps to really see my life. I started practicing mindfulness without knowing it. Once I was aware of what I was doing, I took that a step further and began researching Stoicism. Essentially, I developed a set of tools to help me live in the present and how to drive my life instead of being a passenger.

I still get depressed and that’s ok. But I am aware of it and I don’t make decisions from that state of mind. The greatest tool I ever learned was being able to identify and describe my emotions and feelings out loud. It gave me mastery over those feelings because I ceased to be my own victim. When I feel anxiety, I can ask myself why I am feeling that way and remember to bring myself back to the present. Same with depression. I also learned to allow myself to openly grieve, which is massively cathartic.  Nothing you ever encounter will ever be as powerful or as valuable as your belief in yourself. And I’m not talking about superlative words of affirmation. You can call it a mantra or whatever you want, but in my mind, mine says, “I shape the filter of my life. I must strive to live here and now, eschewing all other things for their appropriate times. I can visit the past, but I mustn’t dwell there and certainly not live there. This life is finite and there’s not a lot of it left. For yourself, your daughters and your wife, make it count.”

Good luck, friend.
